concepts.label: 4/4 time
concepts.definition: A time signature with four quarter-note beats per bar, widely used in popular music and also called common time.

concepts.label: 12/8 time
concepts.definition: A time signature usually felt as four dotted-quarter-note beats per bar, each divided into three eighth notes.

concepts.label: Shuffle
concepts.definition: A repeated long-short subdivision pattern, commonly based on triplets and widely used in blues, boogie-woogie, and related styles.

concepts.label: Laid-back feel
concepts.definition: A timing approach in which notes sit slightly behind the expected beat, creating a relaxed or spacious groove.

concepts.label: Backbeat
concepts.definition: A strong accent on the second and fourth beats of a four-beat bar, commonly played on the snare drum in popular music.

concepts.label: Fast tempo
concepts.definition: A fast musical pulse; Soundlore uses roughly 115-150 BPM as a descriptive guide, with perceived speed varying by musical context.

concepts.label: Very fast tempo
concepts.definition: A very fast musical pulse; Soundlore uses roughly above 160 BPM as a descriptive guide rather than a universal boundary.

concepts.label: Basic rock beat
concepts.definition: A common rock groove combining a steady cymbal subdivision with kick-drum support and snare accents on beats two and four.

concepts.label: Double bass drumming
concepts.definition: Drumming that uses two bass drums or a double pedal to produce rapid, repeated, or interlocking kick-drum strokes.

concepts.label: Gallop rhythm
concepts.definition: A repeated rhythmic figure commonly played as an eighth note followed by two sixteenth notes, especially on guitar or bass drum.

concepts.label: Train beat
concepts.definition: A snare-driven groove whose repeated accents suggest the motion of a train, common in country and rockabilly.

concepts.label: Afrobeat drumming
concepts.definition: Layered, syncopated drumming that combines funk-like grooves with West African rhythmic approaches, closely associated with Afrobeat.

concepts.label: Minor key
concepts.definition: A tonal organization centered on a minor tonic chord, often drawing on natural, harmonic, and melodic minor resources.

concepts.label: Power chord
concepts.definition: A chord voicing built mainly from a root and perfect fifth, often doubled at the octave and lacking a third.

concepts.label: Dominant seventh chord
concepts.definition: A chord combining a major triad with a minor seventh, often used to create harmonic tension or a blues color.

concepts.label: Twelve-bar blues
concepts.definition: A twelve-measure blues framework organized around tonic, subdominant, and dominant harmonies, with many rhythmic and harmonic variants.

concepts.label: I–♭VII–IV progression
concepts.definition: A repeating I-bVII-IV chord pattern that draws on Mixolydian-scale relationships and is common in rock-oriented harmony.

concepts.label: Natural minor scale
concepts.definition: A seven-note scale with the interval pattern whole-half-whole-whole-half-whole-whole, equivalent to the Aeolian mode.

concepts.label: Pentatonic scale
concepts.definition: A scale containing five distinct pitches within an octave, found in many musical traditions and several different interval patterns.

concepts.label: Minor pentatonic
concepts.definition: A five-note scale corresponding to degrees 1, b3, 4, 5, and b7, widely used in blues and rock improvisation.

concepts.label: Blues scale
concepts.definition: A scale commonly formed by adding a chromatic blue note to a pentatonic collection, with several major and minor variants.

concepts.label: Phrygian mode
concepts.definition: A minor-type diatonic mode with a lowered second degree, corresponding to 1, b2, b3, 4, 5, b6, b7.

concepts.label: Hook
concepts.definition: A memorable musical or lyrical idea designed to attract attention and remain recognizable after listening.

concepts.label: Riff
concepts.definition: A short, recurring instrumental figure that provides rhythmic, melodic, or harmonic identity to a piece.

concepts.label: Ostinato
concepts.definition: A musical pattern repeated persistently, often providing a stable foundation beneath changing material.

concepts.label: Topline
concepts.definition: The principal vocal melody, often written together with lyrics over an existing instrumental backing track.

concepts.label: Blue note
concepts.definition: A pitch inflection associated with blues expression, often involving flexible or lowered versions of the third, fifth, or seventh scale degree.

concepts.label: Chorus
concepts.definition: A recurring central section of a song, usually carrying its main hook and relatively stable lyrics.

concepts.label: Guitar solo
concepts.definition: A passage featuring guitar as the principal melodic voice, whether improvised, composed, acoustic, or electric.

concepts.label: Verse–chorus form
concepts.definition: A song structure built around alternating verses and recurring choruses, sometimes including an introduction, bridge, and outro.

concepts.label: Strophic form
concepts.definition: A form that uses the same music for successive verses or stanzas of text.

concepts.label: Power ballad
concepts.definition: A popular-music ballad that develops from a restrained opening into an intense arrangement with prominent drums and amplified instruments.

concepts.label: Harmonized lines
concepts.definition: Melodic lines performed together at different pitches, often maintaining parallel or coordinated harmonic intervals.

concepts.label: Call and response
concepts.definition: A musical exchange in which one phrase is answered by another performer, group, or instrumental part.

concepts.label: Male vocals
concepts.definition: Vocals performed by male singers; the descriptor does not specify a particular pitch range, technique, or timbre.

concepts.label: Tenor
concepts.definition: A relatively high voice type conventionally classified among male singing voices.

concepts.label: Gospel choir
concepts.definition: A choir performing gospel-oriented music, often using expressive harmonies, rhythmic emphasis, and exchanges between soloist and ensemble.

concepts.label: Gang vocals
concepts.definition: A group vocal sound created by several performers shouting or singing together, often loosely in unison.

concepts.label: Head voice
concepts.definition: A vocal-register and resonance term commonly used for a lighter or higher singing quality; its precise meaning varies among teaching traditions.

concepts.label: Belting
concepts.definition: A powerful, speech-like singing quality used at relatively high pitches, shaped by specific resonance and vocal coordination.

concepts.label: Vocal vibrato
concepts.definition: A regular oscillation around a sung pitch, contributing to vocal color, expressiveness, and sustained-note shaping.

concepts.label: Raspy vocals
concepts.definition: A vocal timbre with audible roughness or distortion; several different vocal mechanisms can produce this quality.

concepts.label: Twang
concepts.definition: A bright, concentrated vocal quality associated with particular resonance adjustments, often heard in country and other contemporary styles.

concepts.label: Shriek
concepts.definition: A piercing, high-register harsh vocal sound often associated with black metal.

concepts.label: Vocal harmonies
concepts.definition: Two or more vocal parts sounding together at different pitches to create chordal or contrapuntal relationships.

concepts.label: Acoustic guitar
concepts.definition: A guitar whose hollow body projects string vibrations acoustically, with steel-string and nylon-string designs among its common types.

concepts.label: Electric guitar
concepts.definition: A guitar whose string vibrations are converted into electrical signals by pickups, allowing amplification and extensive sound processing.

concepts.label: Clean electric guitar
concepts.definition: An electric-guitar sound with little audible clipping or distortion, preserving a relatively clear attack and pitch definition.

concepts.label: Distorted guitar
concepts.definition: A guitar sound altered by clipping or saturation, adding harmonics, sustain, compression, and a rougher timbre.

concepts.label: Twelve-string guitar
concepts.definition: A guitar with six paired courses of strings, commonly combining unison and octave pairs for a rich, shimmering sound.

concepts.label: Pedal steel guitar
concepts.definition: A steel guitar played horizontally, with pedals and knee levers that change string pitches while a bar stops the strings.

concepts.label: Electric bass
concepts.definition: A low-register amplified string instrument, commonly played with fingers or a pick to provide rhythmic and harmonic support.

concepts.label: Banjo
concepts.definition: A plucked string instrument with strings stretched over a membrane-covered resonating body, producing a bright, percussive sound.

concepts.label: Fiddle
concepts.definition: A name for the violin in many folk and popular traditions, emphasizing repertory and playing style rather than a separate basic instrument design.

concepts.label: String section
concepts.definition: A group of bowed string players within an ensemble, commonly including violins, violas, cellos, and double basses.

concepts.label: Harmonica
concepts.definition: A free-reed mouth instrument sounded by blowing and drawing air, with pitch and expression shaped by breath and mouth position.

concepts.label: Horn section
concepts.definition: A coordinated group of brass and sometimes woodwind players providing riffs, chords, accents, or melodic lines.

concepts.label: Piano
concepts.definition: A keyboard instrument in which hammers strike strings, allowing changes in loudness through the player's touch.

concepts.label: Honky-tonk piano
concepts.definition: A piano sound associated with honky-tonk settings, often featuring bright attack and slightly detuned or deliberately rough tuning.

concepts.label: Hammond organ
concepts.definition: An electric organ originally using rotating tonewheels, commonly associated with drawbar tone shaping and rotary-speaker effects.

concepts.label: Combo organ
concepts.definition: A portable electronic organ associated with popular music, especially 1960s rock, using transistor-based sound generation.

concepts.label: Synthesizer
concepts.definition: An electronic instrument that creates and shapes sound through oscillators or other sound sources, modulation, and processing.

concepts.label: Drum machine
concepts.definition: An electronic instrument or software system that programs and plays percussion patterns using synthesized or sampled sounds.

concepts.label: Drum kit
concepts.definition: A collection of drums and cymbals arranged for one performer, commonly including kick, snare, toms, and hi-hat.

concepts.label: Tambourine
concepts.definition: A handheld frame instrument with jingles, often also fitted with a drumhead, sounded by striking, shaking, or rubbing.

concepts.label: Cowbell
concepts.definition: A metal percussion instrument struck with a stick, often providing repeated timekeeping or syncopated patterns.

concepts.label: Handclaps
concepts.definition: Percussive sounds produced by striking the hands together, used for rhythmic accents, accompaniment, or communal participation.

concepts.label: Orchestra
concepts.definition: A large instrumental ensemble typically combining strings, woodwinds, brass, and percussion, though its makeup varies by repertory.

concepts.label: Rock band
concepts.definition: An ensemble performing rock-oriented music, commonly built around guitars, bass, drums, and vocals, sometimes with keyboards or other instruments.

concepts.label: Solo performer
concepts.definition: A musician performing alone, possibly singing, playing an instrument, or combining several musical roles.

concepts.label: Palm muting
concepts.definition: A guitar or bass technique in which the picking-hand palm lightly damps the strings near the bridge, shortening and darkening their sound.

concepts.label: Alternate picking
concepts.definition: A picking technique that alternates downstrokes and upstrokes for successive notes.

concepts.label: String bending
concepts.definition: A technique that raises a string's pitch by pushing or pulling it sideways, allowing expressive transitions and inflections.

concepts.label: Slide guitar
concepts.definition: A guitar technique using a slide or bar against the strings to create continuous pitch movement and sustained notes.

concepts.label: Fingerpicking
concepts.definition: A guitar or related string technique using individual fingers to pluck separate strings or coordinated patterns.

concepts.label: Jangle guitar
concepts.definition: A bright, ringing guitar sound produced through clear attacks, sustained open strings, and often arpeggiated chords or twelve-string instruments.

concepts.label: Shred guitar
concepts.definition: A virtuosic guitar approach emphasizing speed, precise articulation, and demanding techniques such as rapid picking, legato, and tapping.

concepts.label: Drop tuning
concepts.definition: A guitar or bass tuning in which the lowest string is lowered relative to the other strings, changing low-register range and chord shapes.

concepts.label: Boogie-woogie bass
concepts.definition: A repeated left-hand piano bass pattern supporting a blues-based groove, often using rolling or broken-chord figures.

concepts.label: Polished production
concepts.definition: A polished production aesthetic emphasizing controlled recording, editing, balance, and clarity; it does not require a particular loudness or dynamic range.

concepts.label: Raw production
concepts.definition: A recording aesthetic that preserves directness, performance irregularities, and relatively limited editing or processing.

concepts.label: Tremolo effect
concepts.definition: A periodic variation in sound level, distinct from vibrato, which varies pitch.

concepts.label: Overdrive
concepts.definition: A form of distortion associated with driving an amplifier or modeled circuit beyond its clean range, often producing comparatively soft clipping.

concepts.label: 1960s sound
concepts.definition: A production aesthetic referencing selected 1960s recording traits, such as tape-based tracking, distinctive room or plate reverberation, and experimental studio layering.

concepts.label: 1970s sound
concepts.definition: A production aesthetic referencing selected 1970s recording traits, such as analog multitracking, distinctive drum-room sounds, and warm electric instrumentation.

concepts.label: 1980s sound
concepts.definition: A production aesthetic referencing selected 1980s traits, often including drum machines, synthesizers, digital reverberation, and strongly processed drums.

concepts.label: 1990s sound
concepts.definition: A production aesthetic referencing selected 1990s traits, such as sample-based production, prominent alternative-rock guitars, or early digital processing, depending on style.

concepts.label: Soft dynamics
concepts.definition: Playing or singing at a comparatively quiet level, with its expressive effect depending on timbre, context, and contrast.

concepts.label: Loud dynamics
concepts.definition: Playing or singing at a comparatively strong level, often creating emphasis or intensity without necessarily implying distortion.

concepts.label: Dynamic contrast
concepts.definition: A marked difference in loudness or intensity between musical passages, parts, or successive events.

concepts.label: Storytelling
concepts.definition: Lyrics that develop events, characters, or a narrative perspective, whether through a clear sequence or fragmented scenes.

concepts.label: Protest lyrics
concepts.definition: Lyrics that criticize, challenge, or mobilize around social or political conditions, often expressing demands or collective concerns.

concepts.label: Abstract lyrics
concepts.definition: Lyrics that emphasize imagery, ambiguity, association, or sound rather than a straightforward narrative or explicit literal message.

concepts.label: Bright and happy
concepts.definition: A perceived cheerful or light musical character, often suggested by buoyant rhythm, clear timbres, or lively phrasing rather than any single technical feature.

concepts.label: Dark
concepts.definition: A musical character perceived as shadowed, somber, or heavy, shaped by timbre, harmony, register, and context.

concepts.label: Aggressive
concepts.definition: A musical character emphasizing force, confrontation, or abrasive energy through performance, rhythm, dynamics, or timbre.

concepts.label: Energetic
concepts.definition: A musical character perceived as active and vigorous, supported by rhythmic drive, strong attacks, or sustained intensity.

concepts.label: Hypnotic
concepts.definition: A musical character that encourages sustained absorption through repetition, steady pulse, gradual change, or immersive texture.

concepts.label: Epic
concepts.definition: A musical character suggesting large scale, grandeur, or dramatic stakes, often created through broad gestures and accumulating intensity.

concepts.label: Anthemic
concepts.definition: A bold, memorable musical character suited to collective participation, often using strong hooks and emphatic recurring phrases.

concepts.label: Romantic
concepts.definition: A musical character associated with affection, intimacy, or emotional longing, distinct from the historical Romantic period.

concepts.label: Playful
concepts.definition: A light, mischievous, or humorous musical character, often created through unexpected gestures, buoyant rhythms, or contrasting sounds.

concepts.label: Introspective
concepts.definition: A musical character perceived as inward-looking or reflective, often supported by restrained delivery and space for detailed expression.
